findings.question: Q1
findings.finding: North America stayed soft through PepsiCo's Q3 (mid-June to 5 Sept). US gasoline averaged about $3.98/gal over the quarter against $3.13 a year earlier, so the Q2 headwind management blamed did not ease. JPMorgan (09-29) says tracked-channel data shows NA underperforming management's plan. PepsiCo is partly reversing its February price cuts after they failed to grow sales (Bloomberg, 09-24). Read: PFNA organic about -2% rather than the -1% Zacks models.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-09: revenue beat with PFNA organic -2% and NA organic -0.5%, stock -3.26%. 2026-04-16: PFNA organic +1% with volume +2%, stock +2.28% (baseline history; Q1/Q2 2026 releases).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The 09-28/09-29 downgrades and the 09-24 price-hike story put NA softness in the wire, and the stock sits at a 52-week low. The residual is the gap between the -1% PFNA model (Zacks, 10-05) and about -2%. If this were fully priced, PFNA consensus would sit near -2% and previews would not frame Oct 8 as a test of whether NA foods volume grows.
findings.independence: Counterparties point the same way on the category and the other way on Frito-Lay's share. Utz: salty category retail sales +0.8% in the 13 weeks to 28 June, down from +2.4% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1739566/000162828026052888/pressrelease-2026q2earning.htm). Casey's: inside comps +3.2% for May-July, so c-stores are not collapsing (https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/caseys-announces-first-quarter-results-2026-09-08). Sized net of these. findings.question: Q2
findings.finding: Input costs moved sharply against PepsiCo after the 9 July call that put FY2026 EPS 'towards the low end'. Brent 78.0 to 100.6 (+29%). ULSD diesel 3.66 to 4.57 (+25%, and +96% against the Q4-2025 average), landing in a 16-week North America Q4 that has to deliver about +9-10% constant-currency EPS. Corn +17%, sugar +38%, 10-year yield +70bp to 5.27%. This raises the odds the release trims FY core constant-currency EPS below +4%. Offsets: about 1 point of tariff refunds already being received, Q3 FX of about +1 point, record productivity, and peers GIS (09-23) and CAG (09-30) both held their full-year guides in the same tape.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-04-24 guidance cut: -4.89%. 2025-02-04 weak guide: -4.51%. 2026-07-09 reaffirmed with a low-end tilt: -3.26%. 2025-07-16 reaffirmed after a cut, on low expectations: +7.45% (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. JPM (09-29) and RBC (10-06) flag transport and freight costs, and the stock is at a 52-week low. But Q3 consensus ($2.30) has been flat for 30 days, and no preview I found quantifies the oil and diesel move since the July call against the Q4 the guide relies on. If this were fully priced, FY consensus would sit below the $8.55 low end and previews would be asking how big the cut is, not whether the guide is reaffirmed.
findings.independence: PepsiCo's own spokesperson tied the coming price increases to commodity and packaging costs and to oil lifted by the regional conflict (Reuters, https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/09/30/pepsico-to-raise-some-chip-prices-as-input-costs-bite). Conagra said its inflation is moving to the high end of 5-6% (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/conagra-brands-inc-cag-q1-010048311.html). Both are separate from the futures data. lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (a refund is noise next to the guide; a finding inside what management guided goes toward 0): F3 (Q3 EPS) cut from +0.2 to +0.1. The beat rests on a pre-announced tariff refund and FX.

Lessons 3/5 (your own caveat reaches the number; a proxy sized against the broader series): F1 (NA) cut from -0.4 to -0.3. Campbell's and Utz share losses and Casey's +3.2% inside comps argue Frito-Lay is gaining share even as its revenue falls.

Lesson 6: bar confirmed from two agreeing estimate sources ($2.30 TipRanks/MarketBeat, $2.29 Zacks) plus the company guide. All findings resolve on 2026-10-08; the late-2026 NA structure update stays in outside_window.
Lesson 7: short interest 1.9% with 3.2 days to cover, so no crowded short to shrink against; no skew available to test the sign.

Left standing: F2 (guide tail) at -0.5, already sized net of the GIS/CAG reaffirmations and the refund/FX offsets. abs_move 4.5 and p_up 45 unchanged after weighing the 'asking what was missed generates pessimism' note against post-call evidence. Sum -0.7 before and after.

investment_decision.reason: The three questions that carry this reaction (NA organic, the FY guide, Q3 EPS) all land at or just past their priced answers. NA softness and the low-end guide were priced in by the 09-28/09-29 downgrades and the 09-24 price-hike reports, and Q3 EPS rests on a pre-announced tariff refund. The one unpriced tilt, input costs up sharply since the July call, makes a guide trim likelier, but it is a macro inference worth about half a point against a 3.75% implied move. The peer tape cuts both ways: GIS and CAG held their guides, and CAG and CPB were sold anyway.
investment_decision.what_would_change_it: The FY2026 guide (Q2). If PepsiCo formally lowers core constant-currency EPS growth below the +4% low end, the short was the trade, likely -4% to -6% on the reaction history.
